venue_now: COLM 2026: every page header reads 'Published as a conference paper at COLM 2026' (p.1); arXiv 2503.05061v4, 28 Sep 2026
what_it_is: A study of how well LLM judges assess correctness rather than style (p.1). Financial professionals wrote BFF-Bench (80 conversations, 160 questions, with long-form expert references) and then judged the correctness of 1,200 responses from several LLMs on BFF-Bench and a hard subset of MT-Bench; these expert verdicts (VERDICTS) are compared with automated graders (p.1-2). Judges are compared under reference conditions: None, Self (an unverified reference the judge writes), Human (an expert-written correct reference), and deliberately wrong or random references (p.2, p.6, p.9). Without a correct reference, judges agree with experts mainly on questions they can answer themselves; an expert reference largely closes the gap, and a slightly incorrect reference can be worse than none (p.1, p.9-10).
domain: business and finance; MT-Bench subset (math, reasoning, coding)
source_of_items: expert-written (financial professionals) plus an MT-Bench subset
evaluation: agreement of automated graders with expert correctness verdicts (p.1-2)
human_validation: the expert verdicts are the ground truth (p.1)

engtrace_use.explanation: The pattern is right (p.1), but the condition is a correct reference, not any reference: a reference the judge writes itself does not help (the Self condition, p.2, p.6), and 'providing slightly incorrect references can be worse than providing no reference at all' (p.10). overlap_with_engtrace: It supports EngTrace's choice of judge inputs, by analogy. The residual judge receives, for each milestone the deterministic check missed, its id and expected value, but not the gold solution (full_run_28092026/judge.py, lines 9-12). Those values are computed by the template code and the gold is verified correct (2,250 of 2,250, state brief section 2), so the judge is in this paper's correct-reference condition and never depends on solving the problem itself. Two limits on the analogy: the paper's references are full long-form answers, while EngTrace gives values without the method; and its task is correctness of whole responses, not whether a trace reaches one value. The paper's warning about slightly wrong references is a reason to keep citing the gold's validation next to the judge.
notes: The venue is confirmed by the paper's own header, so it is not a single-source venue.
